docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
• punishments:add(target: Player|string, invoker: Player|string, type: string, duration?: number, reason: string, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string), hidden?: boolean) Creates a punishment in current provider/service/server scope. hidden (trailing the callback) marks the punishment as hidden from non-privileged views.

  • punishments:addex(target: Player|string, invoker: Player|string, type: string, duration?: number, reason: string, scopes: table, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string), hidden?: boolean) Creates punishment with explicit scopes. scopes is a list of {provider_id: number?, service_id: number?, server_id: number?} tables, each entry becomes one row in bsa_punishment_links. Fails with "no scopes provided" if empty. hidden is the trailing boolean.

  • punishments:revoke(id: number, revoker: Player|string, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Sets revoker_id and removes active entry from local identifier cache.

  • punishments:remove(id: number, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Hard-deletes punishment row.

  • punishments:exist_by_id(id: number, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Fetches one punishment by punishment_id.

  • punishments:exist(identifier: string, callback?: function(entries|false, err?: string)) Fetches all punishments for identifier filtered by current scope.

  • punishments:active(identifier: string, callback?: function(entries|false, err?: string)) Fetches only currently active punishments for identifier filtered by current scope.

  • punishments:rereason(id: number, new_reason: string, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Updates reason and refreshes cached row copy.

  • punishments:reduration(id: number, new_duration?: number, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Updates duration (NULL for permanent) and re-sorts cached entries.

  • punishments:rehidden(id: number, new_hidden: boolean, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Toggles the hidden flag and patches the cached row. Broadcasts database.punishments:update.

  • punishments:rescope(id: number, scope: table, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Replaces the punishment's scope links with a single {provider_id?, service_id?, server_id?} scope. Broadcasts database.punishments:rescope.

  • punishments:scope_add(id: number, scope: table, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Adds one scope link. Fails with "scope link already exists" if the link is a duplicate. Broadcasts database.punishments:scope_added.

  • punishments:scope_remove(id: number, link_id: number, callback?: function(entry|false, err?: string)) Removes one scope link by link_id. Refuses to remove the last link ("must keep at least one scope"). Broadcasts database.punishments:scope_removed.

  • punishments:sort(cache: table) Sort helper for cache ordering (permanent entries first, then longest expiry).

  • punishments:invalidate(identifier: Player|string) Clears active cache for identifier.

  • punishments:get(identifier: Player|string): table|false Returns cached active punishments for identifier.

  • punishments:designated(identifier: Player|string, type: string): table|false Returns first cached punishment matching type.

  • punishments:lookup(identifier: string, callback?: function(entries|false, err?: string)) Cached read-through for active punishments (duration refresh window defaults to 1 hour).

docs.title: Runtime Events
docs.text:
• punishments.invalidated(identifier?: string) Fired when the active punishment cache is cleared. identifier is the player's SteamID64, or nil when the entire cache is flushed.

  • punishments.applied(invoker: Player, entries: table) Fired on PlayerInitialSpawn after a player's active punishments have been loaded from cache and are ready for enforcement.

  • punishments.added(entry: table) Fired after a punishment is inserted into the database and appended to the local active cache.

  • punishments.removed(entry: table) Fired after a punishment is hard-deleted from the database.

  • punishments.revoked(entry: table) Fired after a punishment's revoker_id is set and its active cache entry is removed.

  • punishments.updated(entry: table) Fired after a punishment field is mutated in-place (reason or duration updated via rereason/reduration).

  • punishments.expired(entry: table) Fired during the periodic expiration check when a cached entry's expires_at has passed.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
GMod hooks fired alongside the dispatcher events above. Dispatchers are always first-order and used internally by BSA.

  • BSA.Punishments:added(entry: table) Fired after a punishment is inserted and cached. Fires on both the issuing server and interlink receivers within scope.

  • BSA.Punishments:revoked(entry: table) Fired after a punishment is revoked and the active cache entry is removed.

  • BSA.Punishments:removed(entry: table) Fired after a punishment is hard-deleted.

  • BSA.Punishments:expired(entry: table) Fired during the periodic expiration check when an active entry's expires_at has passed.

  • BSA.Punishments:applied(invoker: Player, entries: table) Fired on PlayerInitialSpawn after the player's active punishments are loaded from cache.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• punishments.cache is keyed by player_identifier, with read-through refresh via lookup(...) and hourly cache TTL metadata (retrieve, duration).

  • On interlink.changed, cache is invalidated and online players are rehydrated from active(...), maintaining cross-server cache coherence.

docs.title: SHARED Autocomplete
docs.text:
Command tree completion, argument shadowing and resolver helpers for chatboxes and command lines.

Info

See core/libraries/autocomplete.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Autocomplete.

Based on the command tree from commands:transport(). Caching/networking and permission rules are layered on by the consumer through the :ensure() and :allowed() seams.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: • autocomplete:new(): autocomplete.object Creates an engine with an empty completer registry and no tree.

docs.title: Manager Object
docs.text:
• autocomplete:feed(tree: table): self Sets the command tree to read from.

  • autocomplete:ready(): boolean true once a tree has been fed.

  • autocomplete:complete(input: string, ply?: Player): result Resolves input into a result. ply defaults to LocalPlayer() clientside. When set, entries are filtered through :allowed. Calling the object directly is shorthand for this.

  • autocomplete:suggest(cmd: string, argStr: string): string[] full command lines for tab-completion, empty once a command resolves.

  • autocomplete:shadow(input: string, ply?: Player): string?, number?, descriptor[]? Returns (shadow, activeIndex, arguments) for the resolved command.

  • autocomplete:values(input: string, ply?: Player): string[], number? Opt-in argument value suggestions for custom UIs, from a registered completer or type-based defaults.

  • autocomplete:defaults(arg: table, ply?: Player): string[] Type-based default values: boolean -> true/false, player -> names, select/multi -> flags.options.

  • autocomplete:set(path: string, fn: function): self Registers a custom argument-value completer for a command path. get/remove manage it.

  • autocomplete:prefix(text: string, prefixes: string[]): string, string | false Matches text against a list of prefixesm, returns the matched prefix and the trailing remainder, or false if none match.

  • autocomplete:ensure() Seam called before each lookup, hook lazy fetching/caching here. No-op by default.

  • autocomplete:allowed(ply, entry: table): boolean Seam to hide entries from completions, returns true by default.

  • autocomplete:resolve(tokens: string[]): node?, consumed: number, path: string[], level: table? Walks the tree by tokens, level is the child map for further suggestions.

  • autocomplete:shadow_of(node, path): string / autocomplete:descriptors(node): descriptor[] / autocomplete:fill_children(level, base, partial, ply, out) Lower-level building blocks used by :complete.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Returned from :complete(...).

  • completions - tab-completable matches { text, full, group, node }[]; empty once a command resolves.
  • command - the resolved command node, or false while still typing the path.
  • path - canonical resolved path names.
  • shadow - display-only usage guide string.
  • arguments - descriptors { name, label, optional, description, default }.
  • index - 1-based index of the argument the cursor is on.

docs.title: SHARED Class
docs.text:
Class is a form of object tracking, inheritance, and metamethod overrides. Without the headaches of those private, public, protected, whatever... Extremely light weight and designed to just be simple, nothing crazy.

Info

See core/libraries/class.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

This adds a dedicated table to BSA as Class.

Classes can be constructed in two ways: namecall or :new(). Both of which allows you to pass arguments into the constructor. However, :new() can be overwritten if you need to.

This is used as the base of all BSA related objects that need some form of tracking and inheritable traits.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• This is how we can construct classes 

    local proto = {}

function proto:constructor()
    print("I am constructed!", ...)
end

function proto:destructor()
    print("I am destructed!")
end

local class_proto = class.register("example", proto)
local object = class_proto:new("hello world")
object:destructor()

  • Class allows for metamethod overrides 

    local __index = {
    ex = true
}
local proto = {}
proto.__index = __index

function proto:constructor()
    print("I am constructed!", ...)
end

function proto:destructor()
    print("I am destructed!")
end

local class_proto = class.register("example", proto)
local object = class_proto:new("hello world")
object:destructor()
print(object.ex) -- true

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
• class.register(name: string, properties: table, base?: table): class.class This registers a new "object" that can be constructed later on with either :new() or just __namecall.

  • class.static(name: string, properties: table, base?: table): class.static This registers a new "object" without a constructor or destructor, useful for just tracking.

  • class.singleton(name: string, properties: table, base?: table): class.object Similar to class.register but immediately constructs it.

  • class.base(object: class.class | class.static | class.object): class.class Returns the base of the object, typically used in recursively traversing back to abstraction.

  • class.baseinvoke(object: class.class | class.static | class.object, method: string, ...: any): ...any Fetches and execute a base class function, useful for recursive functions that need its parent called.

  • class.is_class(object: any): boolean Checks if any type of value is considered part of the class library and is not constructed

  • class.is_object(object: any): boolean Checks if any type of value is considered part of the class library and is constructed

docs.title: SERVER Commands
docs.text:
Runtime command tree system with pluggable interfaces, argument parsing/validation, permission hooks, and recursive group routing.

Info

See core/libraries/command.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Commands.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: • commands:new(): commands.object Creates a command manager, registers baseline argument types, and initializes dispatchers.

docs.title: Manager Object
docs.text:
• commands:phrase(key: string, ...): string Resolves text from manager.phrases and applies string.format when arguments are provided.

  • commands:argument(name: string, callback: function): commands.argument Registers/replaces an argument parser by name.

  • commands:handle(interface: commands.interface, entity?: any): commands.invoker Creates an invoker bound to interface + source entity/custom data.

  • commands:interface(name: string, struct?: table): commands.interface Creates an interface instance and optionally overrides methods with struct.

  • commands:add(name: string): commands.functional Adds/replaces a root-level functional command.

  • commands:remove(name: string) Removes a root-level command/group entry.

  • commands:group(name: string): commands.group Gets or creates a root-level command group.

  • commands:flatten(children?: table, out?: table): table Returns flattened ordered list of groups/commands recursively.

  • commands:transport(children?: table, out?: table): table Builds a serializable tree snapshot (name, aliases, args, desc, permissions, flattened flags).

  • commands:find(...path: string): commands.functional | false Finds nested functional command by exact path segments.

Argument utilities: - argument:destructor() - argument:phrase(key, ...): string

docs.title: Built-In Arguments
docs.text:
Registered by commands:baseline().

  • number tonumber parse with flags.min, flags.max, flags.round, flags.default, flags.optional.

  • string Supports quoted multi-word parsing; optional/default behavior.

  • select Single value from flags.options.

  • multi Comma-separated values from flags.options; supports flags.min/flags.max.

  • boolean Truthy only for "1" or "true" (string forms); otherwise false/default/optional path.

  • color Accepts R,G,B[,A] or hex #RRGGBB[AA].

  • vector Accepts X,Y,Z.

  • angle Accepts P,Y,R.

  • time Accepts absolute seconds or tokenized units (y, mo, w, d, h, m, s). Helper exposed as commands.to_seconds(value).

  • player Supports selector expressions with RPN operators +, -, !, parentheses. Supports prefixes: @ aimed player, ^ self, * all, $ steam id lookup, # usergroup, & radius, ? random count. Flags include single, limit, filter, default, optional.

  • entity Same expression model as player, but for entities. Prefixes: @ aimed entity, ^ self entity, * all entities, # class find, $ entity index, & radius.

  • steam Accepts SteamID, SteamID64, or profile URL. ^ resolves invoker steamid64.

docs.title: SHARED Configurate
docs.text:
Hierarchical, class-driven configuration tree with runtime validation, import/export, exposure-safe snapshots, and change/event dispatching.

Info

See core/libraries/configurate.lua for the actual design implementation.

Warning

Due to how configurate stores data of non-referenced configs, the size may increase from adding/removing configs. You can clean them by calling prune which is for deleting the non-referenced configs, this will however delete that data forever.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Config.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: • configurate:new(): configurate.object Creates a configuration manager with built-in classes and event dispatchers.

docs.title: Manager Object
docs.text:
Root controller and root container for all configuration nodes.

  • configurate:get(...path: string): any Finds a node by path and returns node:get().

  • configurate:set(value: any, ...path: string): boolean, string? Finds a node by path and calls node:set(value).

  • configurate:find(...path: string | string[]): configurate.proxy? Finds a node by path.

  • configurate:add(class: string, name: string, options?: table): configurate.proxy Alias of proxy :add(...) on the manager root.

  • configurate:condition(cfg: configurate.proxy, old: any, new: any): boolean, string? Global condition hook used by every node:set(...). Default returns true.

  • configurate:flatten(children?: table, out?: configurate.proxy[]): configurate.proxy[] Recursively collects child nodes.

  • configurate:export(): table Returns shallow copy of manager registry (includes private/internal metadata).

  • configurate:expose(): table Returns shallow copy of manager exposure (transport-safe metadata view).

  • configurate:import(data: table) Imports child datasets into existing children by key.

  • configurate:prune(): number Intended to prune stale nodes at root.

  • configurate:count(): number, number Intended to count active/inactive nodes at root.

  • configurate:register(name: string, struct: table) Registers a new configuration class inheriting from configurate.proxy.

docs.title: Manager Events
docs.text:
All are dispatcher instances. Callback returns are ignored.

  • configurate.added(parent: configurate.proxy | configurate.object, child: configurate.proxy)
  • configurate.removed(node: configurate.proxy, absolute?: boolean)
  • configurate.changed(node: configurate.proxy, old: any, new: any)
  • configurate.imported(node: configurate.proxy)
  • configurate.exported(node: configurate.proxy)
  • configurate.exposed(node: configurate.proxy)
  • configurate.pruned(node: configurate.proxy, removed_count: number)

docs.title: Proxy Object
docs.text:
Each configuration entry is a configurate.proxy subclass instance.

  • node:add(class: string, name: string, options?: table): configurate.proxy Creates/replaces a named child with the requested class.

  • node:remove(absolute?: boolean) Removes this node from runtime tree. If absolute == true, also removes persisted _c[name] data from parent registry/exposure.

  • node:get(): any Returns stored _v.

  • node:set(value: any): boolean, string? Pipeline order: validate -> override -> debounce -> node:condition -> manager:condition -> commit -> change/events.

  • node:condition(old: any, new: any): boolean, string? Per-node condition hook. Default returns true.

  • node:change(old: any, new: any) Per-node side effect hook after commit. Default no-op.

  • node:override(old: any, new: any): any Per-node mutation hook before debounce. Default returns new.

  • node:debounce(old: any, new: any): boolean, string? Change gate. Default blocks identical non-table values.

  • node:validate(old: any, new: any): boolean, string? Type/rule validator. Default returns true.

  • node:export(): table Shallow copy of node registry + _l absolute path string.

  • node:expose(): table Shallow copy of node exposure + _l absolute path string.

  • node:import(dataset: table, carry?: boolean): boolean, string? Imports node value and child datasets. When carry is false, requires location match (dataset._l == node:path(true)).

  • node:prune(top_level?: configurate.proxy): number Prunes inactive (_r == false) child data recursively and returns removed count.

  • node:count(): number, number Returns recursive active/inactive child counts from registry data.

  • node:restore() Base behavior clears _v in registry/exposure. Built-in typed classes override this to apply defaults through set(...).

  • node:is(...path: string | string[] [, true]): boolean Path comparison helper. If last arg is true, treats comparison as absolute path mode.

  • node:find(...path: string | string[]): configurate.proxy? Finds descendant relative to this node.

  • node:path(concat?: boolean): string[] | string Returns path segments, or dot-joined path when concat == true.

  • node:list(): configurate.proxy[] Returns lineage list from top-level child down to this node.

  • node:flatten(children?: table, out?: configurate.proxy[]): configurate.proxy[] Recursively collects descendants.

docs.title: Proxy Events
docs.text:
All are dispatcher instances. Callback returns are ignored.

  • node.added(listener_node: configurate.proxy, parent: configurate.proxy, child: configurate.proxy)
  • node.removed(listener_node: configurate.proxy, removed_node: configurate.proxy, absolute?: boolean)
  • node.changed(listener_node: configurate.proxy, changed_node: configurate.proxy, old: any, new: any)
  • node.imported(node: configurate.proxy)
  • node.exported(node: configurate.proxy)
  • node.exposed(node: configurate.proxy)
  • node.pruned(listener_node: configurate.proxy, pruned_node: configurate.proxy)

docs.title: Built-In Classes
docs.text:
Registered in constructor via configurate:register(type, struct).

  • container Structure-only node. set(...) always fails with "containers cannot contain values".

  • boolean Value type: boolean. Default options.default or false.

  • number Value type: number. Default options.default or 0. Supports clamp via options.min/options.max.

  • string Value type: string. Default options.default or "". Supports length bounds via options.min/options.max.

  • vector Value type: Vector. Stored as table {x,y,z} internally; get() returns cached Vector. Supports per-axis clamp tables in options.min/options.max.

  • angle Value type: Angle. Stored as table {p,y,r} internally; get() returns cached Angle. Supports per-axis clamp tables in options.min/options.max.

  • color Value type: color-like table (r,g,b[,a]) or Color-style table. Channels are clamped to 0..255; a defaults to 255.

docs.title: Internal Dataset Fields
docs.text:
Serialized trees use these keys:

  • _n: class/type name
  • _c: children map
  • _v: value payload
  • _o: options (exposure side)
  • _r: runtime-active marker (used for pruning)
  • _l: absolute dot path (added by export/expose)

docs.title: SERVER Datastore
docs.text:
Database manager abstraction over multiple SQL engines (currently sqlite and mysqloo) with unified lifecycle/events, query helpers, and optional localized modules.

Info

See core/libraries/datastore.lua for the actual design implementation.

Danger

We highly recommend using transactions and prepared statements for input-based queries. Not doing so will leave you susceptible to SQL injection attacks due to human error.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Datastore.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: • datastore:new(engine: "sqlite" | "mysqloo", config?: table): datastore.object Creates a datastore manager and underlying SQL wrapper instance.

docs.title: Manager Object
docs.text:
• datastore:engine(): datastore.sql Returns underlying engine object.

  • datastore:alive(): boolean Returns connection/alive state from engine.

  • datastore:connect(callback?: function(state: boolean, err?: string)) Starts engine connection flow.

  • datastore:disconnect() Disconnects engine.

  • datastore:type(): string Returns engine class/type name.

  • datastore:query(sql: string, format?: table, callback?: function(data | false, err?: string)) Executes raw query with optional % formatting array. String values in format are escaped automatically.

  • datastore:prepare(sql: string) Returns prepared statement object on engines that support it (mysqloo). SQLite throws unsupported error.

  • datastore:pquery(sql: string, params?: table, callback?: function(data | false, err?: string)) Prepared query shortcut (prepare(...):run(...)) on supporting engines. SQLite throws unsupported error.

  • datastore:transaction() Creates transaction object bound to engine.

  • datastore:escape(value: string, no_quotes?: boolean): string Escapes SQL value through engine implementation.

  • datastore:localize(id: string, struct: table): datastore.localize Registers and constructs a localized module bound to this datastore.

docs.title: Manager Events
docs.text:
All are dispatcher objects. Return values are ignored.

  • datastore.connected(...) Forwarded from engine connected.

  • datastore.disconnected(...) Forwarded from engine disconnected.

  • datastore.queue(query: string | object) Fired when query/statement/transaction query is queued.

  • datastore.failure(err: string) Connection-level failure event.

  • datastore.error(query: string | object, err: string, traceback?: string) Query/runtime error event.

docs.title: SQL Namespace
docs.text:
Engine wrapper registry used internally by datastore:new(...).

  • datastore.SQL.types(): string[] Returns registered engine ids.

  • datastore.SQL.register(id: string, struct: table): class Registers engine class inheriting datastore.sql.

  • datastore.SQL.new(id: string, ...): datastore.sql Constructs registered engine instance.

docs.title: Base Engine Contract (datastore.sql)
docs.text:
Engine wrappers implement/override these methods.

  • engine:connect(callback?)
  • engine:disconnect()
  • engine:alive(): boolean
  • engine:query(sql, format?, callback?)
  • engine:prepare(sql)
  • engine:pquery(sql, params?, callback?)
  • engine:transaction()
  • engine:escape(value, no_quotes?): string
  • engine:type(): string
  • engine:connected(...)
  • engine:disconnected(...)
  • engine:failure(err)
  • engine:error(query, err, traceback?)

docs.title: SQLite Wrapper (sqlite)
docs.text:
• Always alive() == true.
  • connect(cb) is deferred to next tick and immediately succeeds.
  • query(...) executes via sql.Query.
  • prepare / pquery are unsupported and throw errors.
  • escape uses SQLStr.

docs.title: SQLite Query Callback
docs.text:
• Success: callback(data) where data is query result or nil (engine-dependent).
  • Failure: callback(false, sql.LastError()).

docs.title: SQLite Transaction
docs.text:
• tx:query(sql: string, format?: table) Buffers formatted query.

  • tx:pquery(...) Unsupported (throws).

  • tx:count(): number

  • tx:get(): string (newline-joined SQL)
  • tx:trace(): string
  • tx:commit(callback?: function(), wait?: any) Runs buffered queries in transaction. Rolls back on first failure.

docs.title: MySQLOO Wrapper (mysqloo)
docs.text:
Config required in constructor:

  • Host: string
  • Username: string
  • Password: string
  • Schema: string
  • Port: number

Behavior:

  • connect(cb) initializes mysqloo connection and wires native callbacks.
  • disconnect() calls database:disconnect(true).
  • alive() checks mysqloo database status.
  • query(...) returns a mysqloo query object and starts it immediately.
  • prepare(sql) returns statement runner with :run(params, callback?).
  • pquery(sql, params, callback?) is prepare+run shortcut.
  • escape(value, no_quotes?) uses database:escape.

docs.title: MySQLOO Query Object Additions
docs.text:
For normal/prepared query objects created by wrapper:

  • q:get(): string (original SQL text)
  • q:trace(): string (captured traceback)
  • q:isQuery(): true
  • q:isTransaction(): false

docs.title: MySQLOO Query Callback
docs.text:
• Success: callback(data) For multi-query results, callback receives aggregated list of result sets.
  • Failure: callback(false, err) and datastore.error is fired.

docs.title: MySQLOO Prepared Params
docs.text:
Supported parameter types by index:

  • number -> setNumber
  • string -> setString
  • boolean -> setBoolean
  • nil -> setNull

Unsupported types throw an error. Parameter overflow against ? placeholder count throws.

docs.title: MySQLOO Transaction
docs.text:
• tx:query(sql: string, format?: table, callback?: function): self Appends raw query object to transaction.

  • tx:pquery(sql: string, params?: table): self Appends prepared query object to transaction.

  • tx:get(as_string?: boolean): table | string

  • tx:trace(): string
  • tx:count(): number
  • tx:isTransaction(): true
  • tx:isQuery(): false
  • tx:commit(callback?: function(data | false, err?: string), wait?: boolean) Starts transaction and optionally blocks with wait.

docs.title: Localized Storage (datastore.localize)
docs.text:
Per-datastore module class that receives forwarded lifecycle/query events.

Hooks to override:

  • local:connected()
  • local:disconnected()
  • local:queue(query)
  • local:failure(err)
  • local:error(query, err)

Helpers:

  • local:engine()
  • local:alive()
  • local:type()
  • local:query(...)
  • local:prepare(...)
  • local:pquery(...)
  • local:transaction()
  • local:escape(value, no_quotes?)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Query formatting helper escapes only string values passed via format array and then applies string.format.

docs.title: SHARED Dispatcher
docs.text:
Personalized information highways without the need of a global event system. This solves the problem of needing to have hooks everywhere and complicated callback systems.

Info

See core/libraries/dispatcher.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Dispatcher.

Simply create a dispatcher, give it a name, and attach as many callbacks as you need. Names on the dispatchers themselves are for tracking purposes when debugging.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: • dispatcher:new(name: string): dispatcher.object Creates a new dispatcher routine for localized signalling. __namecall also can be used similar to :new.

docs.title: Object
docs.text:
These are returned from calling :new or __namecall. Responsible for holding a collection of handles to fire towards.

  • dispatcher:exists(name: string): boolean Checks if the dispatcher has an existing handle.

  • dispatcher:invoke(...): ...? Executes all stored handles, expecting a return if any exists. A return is made when the first index of any handle's return has value. This will prevent other handles from executing if one returns earlier than others. Errors within callbacks are skipped but still present the error. - dispatcher:fire(...): ...? - dispatcher:call(...): ...? - dispatcher:run(...): ...?

  • dispatcher:connect(callback: function, name?: string): dispatcher.handle Adds a function callback to the designated dispatcher. Not providing a name will make it anonymous, so its important in that note to keep the returned handle if you plan to clean it up later. - dispatcher:listen(callback: function, name?: string): dispatcher.handle - dispatcher:add(callback: function, name?: string): dispatcher.handle - dispatcher:on(callback: function, name?: string): dispatcher.handle

  • dispatcher:disconnect(name: string): boolean Removes a stored handle from the dispatcher. Anonymous dispatchers typically cannot be removed this way unless you managed to get their ID. - dispatcher:dismiss(name: string): boolean - dispatcher:remove(name: string): boolean - dispatcher:off(name: string): boolean

docs.title: Handle
docs.text:
These are returned from dispatcher:connect(...) and represent a single callback entry.

  • handle:invoke(...): boolean, table | string Executes the stored callback through xpcall. - On success: returns true, { ...callbackReturns } - On failure: returns false, traceback - handle:fire(...): boolean, table | string - handle:call(...): boolean, table | string - handle:run(...): boolean, table | string

  • handle:connect(): dispatcher.handle Reconnects this handle to its parent dispatcher. - handle:listen(): dispatcher.handle - handle:add(): dispatcher.handle - handle:on(): dispatcher.handle

  • handle:disconnect(): boolean Disconnects this handle from its parent dispatcher. - handle:dismiss(): boolean - handle:remove(): boolean - handle:off(): boolean

docs.title: SHARED FHTTP
docs.text:
A thin wrapper around the HTTP / CHTTP global that adds automatic retry on failure.

Info

See core/libraries/fhttp.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

FHTTP is an internal helper included locally (include("fhttp.lua")) rather than exposed on the BSA table. It prefers CHTTP when available and falls back to the built-in HTTP.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
• fhttp.HTTP(request: table, attempts?: number) Issues a standard GMod HTTP request and retries up to attempts times (default 2) before invoking request.failed. Wraps the request's success/failed fields to manage retry bookkeeping and clear the registry entry when done.

  • fhttp.fetch(url: string, onsuccess?: function(body: string, length: number, headers: table, code: number), onfailure?: function(err: string), header?: table) GET convenience wrapper built on fhttp.HTTP. The success callback receives the body, its length, the response headers, and the HTTP status code.

  • fhttp.post(url: string, params: table, onsuccess?: function(body: string, length: number, headers: table, code: number), onfailure?: function(err: string), header?: table) POST convenience wrapper built on fhttp.HTTP. params are sent as form parameters; the callbacks match fetch.

docs.title: SHARED Flux
docs.text:
One network string wrapper for multi-channel messaging with SFB/SFS serialization, optional chunk streaming, and built-in replicated variables.

Info

See core/libraries/flux.lua for the actual design implementation.

Note

Garry's Mod has two distinct modes of networking: Reliable & Unreliable. We recommend using Unreliable for non-critical data, like log streaming for example. Doing so relieves pressure on the reliable channel which is used way too often by others.

Note

This adds a dedicated & constructed table to BSA as Flux.

docs.text:

  • flux.sending(encoder: flux.encoder, compressed: string, targets: Player[]) Invoked before standard sends (send, broadcast, omit).

  • SERVER flux.pvsing(encoder: flux.encoder, compressed: string, ...: any) Invoked before :pvs(...).

docs.title: Encoder
docs.text:
Constructed by flux:start(...). Inherits low-level write methods from sfb.Writer.

  • flux.encoder:new(channel?: string, unreliable?: boolean): flux.encoder Creates an encoder instance (explicit constructor form).

  • flux.encoder:clone(): flux.encoder Creates a copy of the encoder with its current write stack, exclusions, inclusions, and streaming state.

  • flux.encoder:fork(): flux.encoder Creates a copy of the encoder's targeting configuration (exclusions, inclusions, streaming) without copying the write stack.

  • flux.encoder:merge(other: flux.encoder): self Appends another encoder's write stack onto this one.

  • flux.encoder:reset(): self Clears current write stack/buffer (also drops any compile cache).

  • flux.encoder:cachable(state?: boolean): self Toggles compile caching (default disabled, omitting state enables it). Disabling drops any existing cache.

  • flux.encoder:cached(): boolean Returns whether caching is enabled and a compiled payload is currently cached.

  • flux.encoder:uncache(): self Drops the cached payload without disabling caching.

  • flux.encoder:compile(): string Returns the compressed payload (util.Compress of the encoded stack). When caching is enabled, reuses the cached result until the write stack length changes.

  • flux.encoder:reliable(state: boolean): self Sets reliability mode (true = reliable, false = unreliable).

  • flux.encoder:isreliable(): boolean Returns reliability state.

  • flux.encoder:channel(channel: string): self Changes target channel and registers it.

  • flux.encoder:size(): number Returns encoded byte length before compression.

  • flux.encoder:table(value: table): self Encodes value through SFS, then writes length + data.

  • flux.encoder:any(value: any): self Encodes any value through SFS, then writes length + data.

  • flux.encoder:stream(state: boolean, capacity?: number): self Enables chunk streaming for large compressed payloads. capacity must be >= flux.stream_minsize.

  • flux.encoder:stream_generate(): number Generates stream id.

  • flux.encoder:stream_status(player?: Player): number Returns stream progress from 0..1 (1 when complete/unknown).

  • SERVER flux.encoder:exclude(...: Player): self Adds players to exclusion list (also removes them from inclusion list).

  • SERVER flux.encoder:include(...: Player): self Adds players to inclusion list (also removes them from exclusion list).

  • SERVER flux.encoder:pas(...): self Sends using net.SendPAS(...). Does not support streaming.

  • SERVER flux.encoder:pvs(...): self Sends using net.SendPVS(...). Does not support streaming.

  • SERVER flux.encoder:broadcast(): self Sends to all humans (with include/exclude adjustments).

  • SERVER flux.encoder:near(position: Vector | Entity, radius: number): self Sends to players within radius of position/entity center.

  • flux.encoder:send(...: Player | Player[]): self Primary send method. Client sends to server via net.SendToServer(), server sends to selected players.

  • SERVER flux.encoder:omit(...: Player): self Sends to human players except the supplied players.

docs.title: Variable Schema
docs.text:
Returned by flux.variables:register(...). Return values are only consumed for onread, ondebounce, oncondition, and onfilter.

  • SERVER schema:onwrite(callback: function(buffer: flux.encoder, entity: Entity | Player | false, value: any)) Overrides write behavior. Expected return: ignored.

  • CLIENT schema:onread(callback: function(buffer: flux.decoder, entity: Entity | Player | false): any) Overrides read behavior. Expected return: decoded value.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
BSA plugins are toggleable feature modules that register themselves with BSA.Plugins:add(...) and then participate in a managed lifecycle.

Info

See core/modules/plugins.lua for the actual design implementation.

  • See Creating a Plugin for the practical authoring guide.
  • See Plugin Runtime Reference for loader behavior, lifecycle, sync, and the manager API.

docs.title: What The Plugin System Gives You
docs.text:
• A per-plugin enable toggle under config.Plugins.<name>.
  • A fresh plugin instance every time the plugin is enabled.
  • Automatic hook cleanup when you use self:add_hook(...).
  • Per-plugin language/config containers created during enable.
  • Server to client syncing of active plugin state.
  • Persistent plugin config storage in data/bsa/config/plugins/<name>.dat.

docs.title: Plugin Shapes
docs.text: You can author plugins in two ways:

docs.title: Single File
docs.text:
Use a single file in lua/bsa/plugins when the plugin is small or mostly shared.

Examples:

  • lua/bsa/plugins/noclip.lua
  • lua/bsa/plugins/whitelist.lua

Top-level files are loaded by filename prefix:

  • sv_*.lua for server-only
  • cl_*.lua for client-only
  • sh_*.lua for shared
  • no prefix defaults to shared

docs.title: Folder Plugin
docs.text:
Use a folder when the client and server parts are large enough to justify separate entry points.

Example:

lua/bsa/plugins/logging/
  sv_init.lua
  cl_init.lua

Folder plugins load these entry files when present:

  • sv_init.lua
  • cl_init.lua
  • sh_init.lua

docs.title: Typical Authoring Flow
docs.text:
1. Pick a stable plugin name. That name becomes the registration key, config key, sync key, and persistence filename.
  2. Create the plugin table and fill in its metadata such as description, config, and optional permissions.
  3. Implement plugin:constructor() for runtime setup.
  4. Register Garry's Mod hooks with self:add_hook(...) instead of raw hook.Add(...).
  5. Clean up non-hook resources in plugin:destructor().
  6. Finish with BSA.Plugins:add("<name>", plugin).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
local plugin = {}
plugin.description = "Allows players with utility.noclip to noclip."
plugin.config = {
    alias = "Noclip",
    permissions = {"management.noclip"},
    sync = true
}
plugin.client_config = {
    alias = "Noclip",
    permissions = {"*"}
}
plugin.permissions = {
    "utility.noclip"
}

function plugin:constructor()
    self:add_hook("PlayerNoClip", self:id(), function(invoker, state)
        if BSA.Players.HasPermission(invoker, "utility.noclip") then
            return true
        end
    end)
end

function plugin:destructor()
end

BSA.Plugins:add("noclip", plugin)

These functions come from libraries/repr.lua and are available on BSA.Repr.

  • repr.typeof(value: any): string Extended type resolver (Color, Entity, Player, etc.).

  • repr.tostring(value: any, is_compact?: boolean): (table, boolean?) Converts a value into a colored expression chunk list. Optional second return marks comma override behavior used by table serializer.

  • repr.tostring_concat(value: any, is_compact?: boolean): string String-only flatten of repr.tostring output (drops colors).

  • repr.stringify(tbl: table, spaces?: number, done?: table, construct?: table): table Builds a colored pretty-print representation of a table (recursive with depth/entry guards).

  • repr.serialize(tbl: table): boolean, table | string Safe table serialization wrapper around stringify (pcall protected).

  • repr.construct(entries: table): table Builds a final printable colored struct from a mixed value list.

  • repr.vararg(...: any): table Shortcut: repr.construct({...}).

  • repr.table(entries: table): table Shortcut: repr.construct(entries).

docs.title: Configuration Tables
docs.text:
• repr.theme: table<string, Color> Named color palette used by converters and constructors.

  • repr.replacements: table<string, string> Escape map used for string display formatting.

  • repr.conversions: table<string, function> Per-type conversion handlers used by repr.tostring.

docs.title: Builder Class (Module Layer)
docs.text:
modules/repr.lua registers repr.class = class.register("repr", repr) and adds constructor helpers:

  • repr.console(...: any): repr.object
  • repr.chat(...: any): repr.object
  • repr.interface(...: any): repr.object
  • repr.custom(...: any): repr.object

Each returns a builder object with internal buffer + network encoder.

docs.title: Builder Object API
docs.text:
• obj:constructor(type: "console" | "chat" | "interface" | "custom", ...: any) Initializes message buffer and network state.

  • obj:reliable(state: boolean): self Sets reliability on underlying network encoder.

  • obj:watermark(): self Prepends [ACRONYM] style watermark. For interface, toggles deferred watermark flag used client-side fallback.

  • obj:insert(...: any): self Prepends entries to buffer. Aliases: first, front.

  • obj:add(...: any): self Appends entries to buffer. Aliases: last, back.

  • obj:build(): self Materializes struct from buffer via repr.table(...), strips leading color in interface mode, and writes payload into network encoder on server.

  • obj:unpack(): ... Returns unpacked built struct.

  • obj:export(): table Returns built struct table.

  • obj:print(): self? Local output behavior by type: - interface (client): UI notification. - chat (client): chat.AddText. - custom: hook.Run("BSA.Repr:custom", struct). - default/console: MsgC(..., "\n").

  • obj:string(): string Returns concatenated string-only content (colors ignored).

  • SERVER obj:channel(): string? Maps builder type to network channel: - chat -> repr.chat - console -> repr.console - interface -> repr.interface - custom -> repr.custom

  • SERVER obj:exclude(...: Player): self Server-only exclusion targeting.

  • SERVER obj:include(...: Player): self Server-only inclusion targeting.

  • SERVER obj:permission(...: string) Sends to players passing BSA.Players.HasPermission(v, ...). Alias: permissions.

  • SERVER obj:group(...: string) Sends to players whose usergroup matches provided groups. Alias: groups.

  • SERVER obj:union(...: string) Sends to players matching either usergroup or permission entries.

  • obj:near(position: Vector | Entity, radius: number): self

  • obj:send(...: Player | Player[]): self
  • obj:broadcast(): self
  • obj:omit(...: Player): self
  • obj:pvs(...: any): self
  • obj:pas(...: any): self Server-side channel send helpers forwarding to underlying network encoder.

docs.title: Network Receive Behavior (Client)
docs.text:
Module registers client receivers:

  • repr.chat -> chat.AddText(unpack(buffer:table()))
  • repr.console -> MsgC(unpack(buffer:table()), "\n")
  • repr.interface -> interface notification, or chat fallback with optional watermark reconstruction
  • repr.custom -> hook.Run("BSA.Repr:custom", buffer:table())

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Table pretty serialization is guarded and can fail-safe to error text via repr.serialize.
  • repr.stringify limits iteration to first 30 keys per table level.
  • Entity/player converters return readable class/name plus runtime index/id when valid.

docs.title: Creating a Plugin
docs.text:
This guide documents the plugin authoring pattern used by the Garry's Mod BSA platform.

If you only need the raw manager API and lifecycle details, see Plugin Runtime Reference.

docs.title: Start With The Right Layout
docs.text:
Use a top-level file when the plugin is small:

lua/bsa/plugins/sh_myplugin.lua

Use a folder when the server and client parts are substantial:

lua/bsa/plugins/myplugin/
  sh_init.lua
  sv_init.lua
  cl_init.lua

The loader supports both forms. Folder plugins are the better choice once the client interface or networking becomes non-trivial, as shown by logging.

docs.title: Step 1: Define And Register The Plugin
docs.text:
Every plugin starts as a plain Lua table and is registered with BSA.Plugins:add(name, plugin).

local plugin = {}
plugin.description = "Controls flashlight usage through BSA permissions."
plugin.config = {
    alias = "Flashlight",
    permissions = {"management.flashlight"},
    sync = true
}
plugin.client_config = {
    alias = "Flashlight",
    permissions = {"*"}
}
plugin.language = {
    alias = "Flashlight"
}
plugin.permissions = {
    "utility.flashlight"
}

What these fields are for:

  • description is descriptive metadata for the plugin.
  • config seeds the top-level config.Plugins.<name> toggle node.
    • setting sync to true allows the config to be networked to clients.
  • (Optional) client_config seeds config.Client.Plugins.<name> when the plugin is enabled on the client.
  • (Optional) language seeds config.Language.Plugins.<name> when the plugin is enabled.
  • (Optional) permissions is a list of permission IDs the plugin introduces. These are registered while enabling when interlink is available.

The registration name should stay stable. Renaming the plugin changes its config path and persisted file name.

docs.title: Step 2: Build Runtime State In constructor
docs.text:
plugin:constructor() runs every time the plugin is enabled. Treat it as runtime setup, not static module initialization.

function plugin:constructor()
    self.language:add("string", "denied", {
        default = "You do not have permission to use flashlight."
    })

    self.cfg_enforce = self.config:add("boolean", "enforce", {
        alias = "Enforce",
        description = "Require utility.flashlight before allowing flashlight usage.",
        default = true
    })
end

During enable, BSA gives your plugin instance these containers:

  • self.config for runtime plugin config
  • self.language for plugin-local language/config phrases
  • self.client_config on the client only

docs.title: Step 3: Use Tracked Hooks, Timers, and Dispatchers
docs.text:
Use self:add_hook(...) instead of raw hook.Add(...). Timers, dispatcher connections, and HTTP requests are also tracked — see Plugin Runtime Reference for the full surface.

function plugin:constructor()
    self:add_hook("PlayerSwitchFlashlight", self:id(), function(invoker, enabled)
        if not self.cfg_enforce:get() then
            return
        end

        if BSA.Players.HasPermission(invoker, "utility.flashlight") then
            return true
        end

        return false
    end)
end

Hook IDs are automatically namespaced as <plugin>.<id>. Everything registered this way is cleaned up automatically on disable through plugin:clean().

docs.title: Step 4: Clean Up What Is Not Tracked
docs.text:
Tracked: hooks, timers (add_timer/simple_timer), dispatcher connections (add_dispatcher), and HTTP requests (self:http). These are released automatically on disable. Not tracked: raw network:receive(...), file handles, global state your plugin mutated.

function plugin:destructor()
    network:receive("plugin.flashlight.sync", nil)
end

docs.title: Step 5: Add Language Phrases
docs.text:
self.language is created for every enabled plugin and supports nested phrase trees.

function plugin:constructor()
    do local notifications = self.language:add("container", "notifications")
        notifications:add("string", "denied", {
            default = "Flashlight usage is not allowed."
        })
    end
end

Then fetch text with:

self.language:phrase("#notifications.denied")
  • #path.to.phrase resolves through the plugin language tree.
  • Extra arguments are passed through string.format.
  • The language tree exists on both server and client.

docs.title: Step 6: Add Client Config Or Interface When Needed
docs.text:
plugin.client_config is only materialized into a config container on the client during enable.

That means self.client_config:add(...) should only be used from client code or behind if CLIENT then.

For interface-heavy plugins, define plugin.interface and keep the implementation clientside.

do local interface = {}
    plugin.interface = interface
    interface.alias = "Flashlight"
    interface.icon = "icon16/lightbulb.png"
    interface.permissions = {"utility.flashlight"}

    function interface:constructor(parent)
        -- build VGUI here
    end

    function interface:destructor()
    end
end

When the plugin enables on the client, BSA mounts that interface through BSA.Interface:add(name, interface). See Interface Overview for how interfaces are handle and their functions. See Interface Overview - Feature about the structure of the interface table.

docs.title: Step 7: Support Realm Separation Deliberately
docs.text:
A few rules make plugin authoring less error-prone:

  • Put server-only storage, database, or authoritative logic in sv_*.lua or sv_init.lua.
  • Put large VGUI and client presentation code in cl_*.lua or cl_init.lua.
  • If you split the plugin by realm, register the same plugin name in each realm entry file.

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
local plugin = {}
plugin.description = "Controls flashlight usage through BSA permissions."
plugin.config = {
    alias = "Flashlight",
    permissions = {"management.flashlight"},
    sync = true
}
plugin.client_config = {
    alias = "Flashlight",
    permissions = {"*"}
}
plugin.permissions = {
    "utility.flashlight"
}

function plugin:constructor()
    self.language:add("string", "denied", {
        default = "You do not have permission to use flashlight."
    })

    self.cfg_enforce = self.config:add("boolean", "enforce", {
        alias = "Enforce",
        description = "Require utility.flashlight before allowing flashlight usage.",
        default = true
    })

    self:add_hook("PlayerSwitchFlashlight", self:id(), function(invoker, enabled)
        if not self.cfg_enforce:get() then
            return
        end

        if BSA.Players.HasPermission(invoker, "utility.flashlight") then
            return true
        end

        return false
    end)
end

function plugin:destructor()
    network:receive("plugin.flashlight.sync", nil)
end

BSA.Plugins:add("flashlight", plugin)

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
• Using raw hook.Add(...) and forgetting cleanup.
  • Calling self.client_config:add(...) from shared/server code.
  • Renaming a plugin after shipping it and then wondering why old config is not picked up.
  • Forgetting to unregister network:receive(...) in destructor() — this is the main thing not auto-cleaned.
